title.narrative: Transforming Vegetable Farming as a Business : Scaling up (Year One)

description.narrative: Increase the capacity of 39,520 farmers by showcasing better yields and profit through using better seed and improved farming practices. This project will position vegetables as an attractive business opportunity for smallholder farmers thereby catalyzing development of a professional vegetable sector while facilitating development of a competitive agri-input market.

The Transforming Vegetable Farming as a Business: Scaling up project builds on the successful implementation of the pilot phase (November 2023–March 2025), during which 7,733 smallholder farmers were trained, generating valuable implementation experience and lessons that informed the design of the current phase of the project.
The scale-up phase of the project is being implemented over a four-year period (July 2025–June 2029) with the objective of increasing the productivity, profitability, and sustainability of smallholder vegetable farming in Ghana. This phase has expanded the project’s geographical coverage from three regions (Bono, Bono East, and Ahafo) to five regions through the inclusion of the Ashanti and Upper East regions. This expansion enables the project to reach a broader and more diverse farmer base, respond to varying agro-ecological conditions, and extend the benefits of improved vegetable production technologies and business-oriented farming practices to more farming communities. The project promotes the adoption of quality seed, good agricultural practices, climate-resilient production techniques, and sound farm business management to enable farmers to achieve higher yields, improve product quality, and increase household incomes.
Implemented by East-West Seed Knowledge Transfer Foundation (EWS-KT) and co-funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN) and East-West Seed (EWS), the project also seeks to strengthen the broader vegetable sector by improving farmers' knowledge on quality agricultural inputs, extension services, and market opportunities. Through strategic partnerships with public- and private-sector actors, the project contributes to the development of a more professional, competitive, and resilient vegetable value chain in Ghana.

sector.narrative: The project in year one (1) implemented impactful initiatives that significantly benefited farmers. Key highlights included the establishment of demonstration plots in 22 districts by our Technical Field Officers (extension personnel), showcasing innovative vegetable farming techniques. Additionally, comprehensive training programs covered essential topics such as land preparation, pest management, business planning, and more, collectively equipping farmers with the knowledge and skills to boost productivity and capabilities.

tag.narrative: By improving agricultural productivity and increasing access to safe-to-eat vegetables, the project contributes to food security and nutrition.
By increasing farmers' incomes and promoting sustainable agricultural practices, the project supports economic growth and decent work.
The project's emphasis on climate-smart production practices helps farmers adapt to climate change and reduces the environmental impact of agriculture.
The project's focus on women and youth farmers promotes gender equality and empowers these groups in the agricultural sector.
